title: NativeLink Workers

panels.title: Worker hosts now

targets.expr: (100 * (max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_internal_bytes{job="node",platform="macos"}) - on(instance, platform) max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_purgeable_bytes{job="node",platform="macos"}) + on(instance, platform) max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_wired_bytes{job="node",platform="macos"}) + on(instance, platform) max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_compressed_bytes{job="node",platform="macos"})) / on(instance, platform) max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_total_bytes{job="node",platform="macos"})) or (100 * (1 - max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes{job="node",platform="linux"}) / on(instance, platform) max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_MemTotal_bytes{job="node",platform="linux"})))

(100 * max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_swap_used_bytes{job="node",platform="macos"}) / on(instance, platform) max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_swap_total_bytes{job="node",platform="macos"})) or (100 * (1 - max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_SwapFree_bytes{job="node",platform="linux"}) / on(instance, platform) (max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_SwapTotal_bytes{job="node",platform="linux"}) > 0)))
max by (instance, platform) (node_load1{job="node"}) / on(instance, platform) count by (instance, platform) (node_cpu_seconds_total{job="node",mode="idle"})

panels.description: Current figures per worker host, macOS and Linux, from node_exporter. CPU and memory turn yellow at 80% and red at 95%; swap at 50% and 80%; load per core at 1.5 and 3. Memory is app plus wired plus compressed on macOS and memory not available to new work on Linux. A Linux host with no swap has an empty swap cell.

panels.title: CPU busy, by worker host
panels.description: Share of CPU time not idle, averaged over all cores.

panels.title: Memory used, by worker host

targets.expr: (100 * (max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_internal_bytes{job="node",platform="macos"}) - on(instance, platform) max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_purgeable_bytes{job="node",platform="macos"}) + on(instance, platform) max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_wired_bytes{job="node",platform="macos"}) + on(instance, platform) max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_compressed_bytes{job="node",platform="macos"})) / on(instance, platform) max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_total_bytes{job="node",platform="macos"})) or (100 * (1 - max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes{job="node",platform="linux"}) / on(instance, platform) max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_MemTotal_bytes{job="node",platform="linux"})))

panels.description: macOS: app (internal minus purgeable) plus wired plus compressed memory, as a share of physical memory. Linux: memory not available to new work (1 - MemAvailable / MemTotal). Sustained high values with rising swap point to memory pressure.

panels.title: Swap used, by worker host

targets.expr: (100 * max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_swap_used_bytes{job="node",platform="macos"}) / on(instance, platform) max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_swap_total_bytes{job="node",platform="macos"})) or (100 * (1 - max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_SwapFree_bytes{job="node",platform="linux"}) / on(instance, platform) (max by (instance, platform) (node_memory_SwapTotal_bytes{job="node",platform="linux"}) > 0)))

panels.description: Share of the swap files in use.

panels.title: Load per core, by worker host

targets.expr: max by (instance, platform) (node_load1{job="node"}) / on(instance, platform) count by (instance, platform) (node_cpu_seconds_total{job="node",mode="idle"})

panels.description: 1-minute load average divided by core count.

panels.title: Paging out to swap, by worker host

targets.expr: (max by (instance, platform) (rate(node_memory_swapped_out_bytes_total{job="node",platform="macos"}[5m]))) or (4096 * max by (instance, platform) (rate(node_vmstat_pswpout{job="node",platform="linux"}[5m])))

panels.description: Bytes written to swap per second (on Linux, pages swapped out times the 4 KiB page size). Sustained non-zero paging means the host is short of memory.

panels.title: Hub host (headcrash, which is also a Linux worker)
Hub CPU busy
panels.description: headcrash runs the hub, cache and scheduler; it is not one of the worker slots.

panels.title: Hub memory used
panels.description: 1 - MemAvailable / MemTotal.

panels.title: Hub swap used
panels.description: Share of swap in use.

panels.title: Hub load per core
panels.description: 1-minute load average divided by core count.

panels.title: Hub pages swapped out per second
panels.description: Pages written to swap per second (node_vmstat_pswpout).

panels.title: Hub OOM kills (24h)
panels.description: Processes the Linux OOM killer ended on headcrash in the last 24 hours.

panels.title: Total slots, by OS
panels.description: Slots offered by the connected workers of each operating system. The hub routes an action on its OSFamily, so the macOS and the Linux workers are two pools: a build can only use the slots of its own.

panels.title: Slots in use (%), by OS
panels.description: Running actions as a share of the slots offered, for each operating system. Yellow from 80%, red when every slot is busy. One pool can be full while the other is idle.

panels.title: Slots offered, by worker
panels.description: How many actions each worker will run at once (max_inflight_tasks in its config), read from the hub's worker list.

panels.title: Slots in use now, by worker
Slots in use over time, by worker
panels.description: A worker pinned at its slot count is full. A worker that drops to zero while others are full has left the pool.

panels.title: Share of each worker's slots in use (%)
Free slots per worker
panels.description: Slots offered minus actions running. Zero everywhere while the queue is non-empty means the pool is saturated.

panels.title: Completed actions per minute, by worker
panels.description: Throughput of each worker. A worker far below the others with the same slot count is slow or starved.

panels.title: Output uploaded, bytes per second, by worker
Completed actions, last hour, by worker
Execution time, median, by worker
panels.description: Time the action's own command ran on the worker, excluding fetching inputs and uploading outputs.

panels.title: Input fetch time, 90th percentile, by worker
panels.description: Time to bring an action's inputs from the hub into the worker's store and stage them.

panels.title: Output upload time, 90th percentile, by worker
Queue wait before dispatch, median, by worker
panels.description: How long the actions that ended up on this worker had waited for a slot.

panels.title: Whole action time (queue to result), 90th percentile, by worker
Killed actions (24h), by action type and outcome
panels.description: KILLED_EXTERNAL is a SIGKILL from outside NativeLink (most likely the OOM killer); KILLED_TIMEOUT is the action timeout. The metric has no worker label, so kills cannot be attributed to a host.

panels.title: Peak memory per action, 99th percentile (24h), top 10 action types
panels.description: Interpolated from coarse buckets (1, 4, 16 GiB), so values near 4 GiB mean 'between 1 and 4 GiB'. No worker label exists on this metric.

panels.title: Queued actions
panels.description: Actions waiting for a worker slot.

panels.title: Unsatisfiable queued actions
panels.description: Queued actions no connected worker can ever run (platform properties match no worker). Anything above zero needs attention.

panels.title: Oldest queued action
panels.description: How long the longest-waiting queued action has waited.

panels.title: Oldest executing action
panels.description: How long the longest-running action has been executing.

panels.title: Retried actions (24h)
panels.description: Actions re-run after losing their worker or failing in a retryable way.

panels.title: Oldest queued and executing action age
Worker registrations (24h)
panels.description: Times a worker registered with the hub in the last 24 hours. Each worker registers once per hub or worker restart; more than the worker count means workers reconnected.

panels.title: Workers draining or paused
panels.description: Workers taken out of rotation by the pool admin.

panels.title: Keepalive gap, 99th percentile (1h)
panels.description: Longest gaps between worker keepalives. The hub drops a worker after 30 s without one (worker_timeout_s), so yellow is half that and red is the timeout.

panels.title: Draining and paused, by worker
panels.description: Pool admin state per worker.

panels.title: Distinct registrations per worker (24h)
panels.description: 1 means the worker has stayed registered for the whole day. Each extra one is a re-registration under a new id. Workers whose id has no host-name prefix (started before workers were named) are grouped as (unnamed).

panels.title: Keepalive gap, 99th percentile
panels.description: Threshold lines at 15 s (half the 30 s worker timeout) and 30 s (the timeout).

description: Per-worker view of the remote-execution pool: the macOS and the Linux workers of the one hub, from the hub's own metrics. The host name is the prefix of the worker id. Host CPU, memory and swap come from node_exporter on each worker host (Prometheus job node, label platform).
